Rashi on Chullin 90a:10:1.hebrew: לישנא אחרינא כאן לחלצו כאן להעלותו - מאן דאמר "אין נוהג בעולה", לחלצו קאמר, שאינו מצווה לחלצו מן הירך; ומאן דאמר "נוהג", להעלותו קאמר, דאסור להעלותו בפני עצמו אם פירש מן הירך:
Rashi on Chullin 90a:10:1.english: Another version: Here, to remove it; there, to bring it up - The one who says [that the prohibition of the sciatic nerve] does not apply to a burnt offering is speaking of removing it, [meaning] that one is not commanded to remove it from the thigh; and the one who says [that it] applies is speaking of bringing it up [onto the altar], [meaning] that it is forbidden to bring it up by itself if it became separated from the thigh:

Rashi on Chullin 90a:11:1.hebrew: רב נחמן בר יצחק אמר לחלצו פליגי - דמ"ד נוהג, קסבר מצוה לחלצו. וללישנא קמא "להעלותו פליגי" — מ"ד נוהג, קסבר להעלותו נמי אסור עם הירך, כדפליגי רבי ורבנן לקמן: דלרבי שרי, כדמוקי לקמן אליבא דרבי, כי איצטריך קרא למשרי גיד הנשה במחובר; ולרבנן אסור, דבעינן "מן המותר לישראל":
Rashi on Chullin 90a:11:1.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said: They disagree [regarding whether it is a mitzvah] to remove it - For the one who says [the prohibition of the sciatic nerve] applies [to consecrated animals] holds that it is a mitzvah to remove it [before burning the thigh]. And according to the first version [of the Gemara, which reads] "they disagree [regarding whether it is permitted] to bring it up": the one who says it applies holds that even bringing it up [onto the altar] with the thigh is forbidden, just as Rabbi [Yehudah HaNasi] and the Rabbis disagree below — for according to Rabbi it is permitted, as [the Gemara] establishes below according to Rabbi that when the verse is needed, [it is] to permit the sciatic nerve while [still] attached [to the thigh]; whereas according to the Rabbis it is forbidden, because we require [that offerings be brought] "from that which is permitted to Israel":

Rashi on Chullin 90a:11:2.english: It all - [This] is an inclusive term:

Rashi on Chullin 90a:12:1.english: Even [if] they became detached - [meaning] those sinews [became detached] from the flesh. It is speaking of permitted sinews, similar to bones:

Rashi on Chullin 90a:14:1.hebrew: ומאן שמעת ליה כו' - כלומר, והך מתניתי' לאו דברי הכל היא, אלא רבי היא, ופליגי רבנן עליה, וכדתניא כו'; ומפלוגתייהו שמעינן דלרבי גיד הנשה מותר, ולרבנן אסור, כדמפרש ואזיל:
Rashi on Chullin 90a:14:1.english: And who [is it] that you heard, etc. - That is to say, this teaching is not [the opinion of] everyone, rather it is [the view of] Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi], and the Rabbis disagree with him — as it is taught [in the baraita], etc.; and from their dispute we learn that according to Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] the sciatic nerve is permitted [to be offered on the altar], while according to the Rabbis it is prohibited, as [the Gemara] proceeds to explain:

Rashi on Chullin 90a:15:1.english: And how do I realize "the flesh and the blood" - [meaning,] and not sinews:

Rashi on Chullin 90a:15:2.english: To [parts] that pop off - [that is,] from atop the fire; [in Old French,] *esclant* [bursting]:

Rashi on Chullin 90a:17:1.hebrew: מידי דהוי אראשה של עולה - דצריך שיקריבנו שלם, כדכתיב (ויקרא א) "ואת הראש", והרי עצמות הרבה יש:
Rashi on Chullin 90a:17:1.english: Just as it is [with] the head of a burnt offering - for one must offer it whole, as it is written (Leviticus 1[:8]), "and the head," and behold, there are many bones [in it]:

Rashi on Chullin 90a:1:1.hebrew: אלמא איסור מוקדשין קדים - דמשעה שנוצר הוא קדוש, ועדיין לא נוצר הגיד, דהא חזינן דיצירת עובר קודמת ליצירת גיד:
Rashi on Chullin 90a:1:1.english: Evidently, the prohibition of consecrated [animals] precedes [it] - for from the moment it is formed, it is consecrated, and the sinew has not yet been formed, for we see that the formation of the embryo precedes the formation of the sinew:

Rashi on Chullin 90a:2:1.hebrew: ומשנינן אע"ג דאיסור מוקדשים קדים אתי איסור גיד וחייל - הואיל ואיסור חמור הוא, שנוהג בבני נח, כדקתני מתניתין (לקמן חולין דף ק:): "והלא לבני נח נאסר גיד הנשה":
Rashi on Chullin 90a:2:1.english: And we answer: Even though the prohibition of consecrated [animals] precedes [it], the prohibition of the [sciatic] nerve comes and takes effect - since it is a stringent prohibition that applies to the descendants of Noah, as the Mishnah teaches (below, Chullin 100b): "Was not the sciatic nerve prohibited to the descendants of Noah?"

Rashi on Chullin 90a:3:1.hebrew: ופרכינן מאן שמעת ליה הא סברא - דנוהג בבני נח — רבי יהודה, בשילהי מתני' (שם):
Rashi on Chullin 90a:3:1.english: And we ask: Who did you hear [holds] this reasoning - that [the prohibition] applies to the descendants of Noah? [It is] Rabbi Yehuda, at the end of the Mishnah (there):

Rashi on Chullin 90a:3:2.hebrew: והאי תנא דרישא דמתניתין דלא כרבי יהודה דקתני בירך של ימין ושל שמאל - ואילו רבי יהודה שמעינן ליה לקמן, דאמר: אינו נוהג אלא באחד:
Rashi on Chullin 90a:3:2.english: And this Tanna of the first clause of our Mishnah is not in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda, as it teaches, "on the right thigh and on the left [thigh]" - Whereas [regarding] Rabbi Yehuda, we hear him [saying] later that he says: It applies only to one [of them]:

Rashi on Chullin 90a:4:1.english: He holds in accordance with him regarding one [matter] - that [the prohibition] applies to the descendants of Noah:

Rashi on Chullin 90a:4:2.english: And disagrees with him on one [matter] - [holding] that [the prohibition] applies to both thighs:

Rashi on Chullin 90a:5:1.hebrew: אימור דשמעת ליה לר' יהודה - דאמר דמשום חומריה דגיד דנוהג בבני נח, חייל נמי אאיסור אחרינא:
Rashi on Chullin 90a:5:1.english: Say that you heard Rabbi Yehuda [say so] - who said that due to the stringency of the [sciatic] nerve, which applies to the descendants of Noah, it also takes effect upon another prohibition:

Rashi on Chullin 90a:5:2.hebrew: בטמאה - שמעת ליה דאתי איסור גיד וחייל אאיסור טמאה, דאע"ג דאיסור טמאה ממעי אמה ואיסור גיד אינו עד שיולד — דהא רבי יהודה "אין נוהג בשליל" קאמר במתניתין — אפילו הכי חייל גיד אטמאה, משום דאיסור טמאה לאו בעלמא הוא, ואיסור גיד חמור שכן נוהג בבני נח:
Rashi on Chullin 90a:5:2.english: With regard to a non-kosher [animal] - you heard [that Rabbi Yehuda holds] that the prohibition of the sciatic nerve comes and takes effect upon the prohibition of a non-kosher [animal]. For even though the prohibition of a non-kosher [animal] [applies] from its mother's womb, whereas the prohibition of the sciatic nerve does not [take effect] until it is born — for Rabbi Yehuda states in the Mishnah, "[It] does not apply to a fetus" — even so, [the prohibition of] the sciatic nerve takes effect upon [the prohibition of] a non-kosher [animal], because the prohibition of a non-kosher [animal] is merely a negative commandment, whereas the prohibition of the sciatic nerve is more stringent in that it applies to the descendants of Noah:

Rashi on Chullin 90a:5:3.hebrew: קדשים דאיסור כרת - שעל ידי קדשים בא לידי כרת, כגון אכלו בטומאה או פגול ונותר:
Rashi on Chullin 90a:5:3.english: Sacrificial [animals], which are a prohibition [punishable by] karet - For through sacrificial [animals] one comes to [incur] karet [excision], such as [if] one ate it in [a state of] ritual impurity, or [as] piggul [disqualified by improper intention] or notar [leftover sacrificial meat]:

Rashi on Chullin 90a:5:4.english: Did you hear him - [say] that [the prohibition of] the sciatic nerve takes effect upon them:

Rashi on Chullin 90a:6:1.hebrew: אלא הכא במבכרת עסקינן - דלא קדוש ולד אלא ברחם ביציאתו. ואשמעינן תנא דידן, דאע"ג דאין גיד נוהג בשאר מוקדשים — דהא איסור מוקדשים קדים, כדאמרת, דיצירת עובר קודמת ותו לא אתי איסור גיד וחייל — אפילו הכי יש מוקדשים שהגיד נוהג בהן, כגון בכור, ממה נפשך: אי נוהג בשליל, איסור גיד קודם ותו לא פקע; ואי אין נוהג בשליל, תרוייהו בהדי הדדי אתו:
Rashi on Chullin 90a:6:1.english: Rather, here we are dealing with [an animal] giving birth to [its] firstborn - For the offspring is only sanctified in the womb upon its emergence. And our Tanna teaches us that even though [the prohibition of] the sciatic nerve does not apply to other consecrated animals — since the prohibition of consecrated [animals] precedes [it], as you said, for the formation of the fetus precedes [it], and the prohibition of the sciatic nerve cannot then come and take effect — nevertheless, there are consecrated animals to which the sciatic nerve [prohibition] does apply, such as a firstborn, either way: if [it] applies to a fetus, the prohibition of the sciatic nerve precedes [sanctification] and does not subsequently depart; and if [it] does not apply to a fetus, both of them come simultaneously:

Rashi on Chullin 90a:7:1.hebrew: ואיבעית אימא בולדות קדשים - ואשמועינן תנא דידן דלא קדשי במעי אמן אלא בהוייתן, ביציאתן. הילכך איסור גיד נוהג בכולן, משום דאיהו קדים, דנוהג בשליל ותו לא פקע; דלא תימא במעי אמן קדושים, ואיסור מוקדשין קדים כדאמרן בנפל שלא נתקשרו אבריו בגידין, ותו לא אתי איסור גיד וחייל. להכי נקט "בהוייתן", משום לישנא דקרא דילפינן מיניה קדושת ולדות קדשים בפ"ב דבכורות (דף יד:): "רק קדשיך" — אלו תמורות, "אשר יהיו לך" — אלו הולדות:
Rashi on Chullin 90a:7:1.english: And if you wish, say [it deals] with the offspring of sacrificial [animals] - And our Tanna teaches us that they are not sanctified in their mother's womb, but rather when they come into being, [meaning] upon their emergence [at birth]. Therefore, the prohibition of the [sciatic] nerve applies to all of them, because it comes first, as it applies to a fetus and then does not depart; so that you should not say they are sanctified in their mother's womb, and [thus] the prohibition of consecrated [animals] comes first, as we said regarding a non-viable fetus whose limbs have not yet been bound together with sinews, and [then] the prohibition of the [sciatic] nerve would no longer come and take effect. For this reason [the Gemara] uses the term "when they come into being" [be-hawayatan], because of the wording of the verse from which we derive the sanctity of the offspring of sacrificial [animals] in the second chapter of Bekhorot (14b): "Only your holy things" — these are substitute [offerings]; "which shall be [yihyu] yours" — these are the offspring:

Rashi on Chullin 90a:8:1.english: [Sacrificial animals] that are eaten - [such as] a sin offering, a guilt offering, and a peace offering:

Rashi on Chullin 90a:8:2.english: That are not eaten - [such as] a burnt offering:

Rashi on Chullin 90a:9:1.english: [With regard] to flogging him - he receives lashes if he ate it:

Rashi on Chullin 90a:9:2.hebrew: להעלותו - למזבח, אין איסור גיד נוהג, כדאמרינן לקמן: דלא כתיב "ולא יאכל המזבח":
Rashi on Chullin 90a:9:2.english: To bring it up - onto the altar, the prohibition of the [sciatic] nerve does not apply, as we say later: for it is not written, "and the altar shall not eat":

Tosafot on Chullin 90a:14:1.hebrew: פרשו ירדו רבי היא דתניא כו' - תימה, אמאי מייתי הך ברייתא קמייתא? ונראה, דאי לאו ברייתא קמייתא, המ"ל דרבנן סברי שיש לרבות כל מה שנוכל לרבות, ואפילו פרשו דאיסורא, ולית לן למעוטי אלא פוקעים גרידא, שהוא סוף העלאה; ורבי סבר דרבויא ומיעוטא אית לן לאוקומי בתחלת העלאה, ולא נמעט כמו כן אלא דבר אחד, דהיינו פרשו דאיסורא, אבל מחוברים דאיסורא ופרשו דהיתירא יעלו. ולהכי מייתי ברייתא קמייתא, דגידים דהיתירא נמי כשפרשו ירדו, דומיא דעצמות דהיתירא, ועל כרחך רבי היא; אלמא לא מרבי רבי כל מה שיכול להרבות, דהא אוקי נמי מיעוט בפרשו דהיתירא. והכי נמי לרבנן, לא מרבי כל מה שיכולין להרבות, אלא ממעטין דאיסורא אפילו במחוברין:
Tosafot on Chullin 90a:14:1.english: [If] they became detached, they shall descend; it is Rabbi, as it is taught, etc. - It is astonishing why [the Gemara] brings this first baraita! And it appears that if not for the first baraita, one could have said that the Rabbis hold that we must include everything we are able to include, even [prohibited sinews] that became detached, and we should exclude only [parts] that merely become dislodged [from the fire], which is at the end of the offering-up; whereas Rabbi holds that we must establish the inclusion and exclusion at the beginning of the offering-up, and we should likewise exclude only one thing — namely, [prohibited sinews] that became detached — while [prohibited sinews] that are attached and [permitted parts] that became detached shall ascend. Therefore, [the Gemara] brings the first baraita, [which indicates] that permitted sinews too, when they became detached, descend — similar to permitted bones — and perforce [that baraita] is [the view of] Rabbi; thus, Rabbi does not include everything that he could include, for behold, he also applied the exclusion to permitted [parts] that became detached. And so too according to the Rabbis: they do not include everything that they could include; rather, they exclude [the] prohibited [sinews] even when attached:

Tosafot on Chullin 90a:1:1.hebrew: אלמא איסור מוקדשין קדים - אומר ר"ת: משום דמתחלה הכל הוא בשר, והבשר עצמו מתקשה אחרי כן ומתלבן ונעשה גיד. ובקונטרס פי' לקמן, דמתחלה כשהגיד נוצר אינו על הכף, ולא חייל עד שיבא ויתקשה על הכף. ואע"ג דהשתא ר"ל דאין איסור גיד חל על איסור מוקדשים, על איסור אבר מן החי, דלא חמיר כמוקדשים, חייל; ועוד, דאי אפשר לאיסור גיד להיות בענין אחר; ועוד, דאין איסור אבר מן החי חל עד שיולד, דאמר בסוף פרקין (לקמן חולין דף קג.): כגון שנטרפה עם יציאת רובה, דאיסור טרפה ואיסור אבר מן החי חייל בהדי הדדי:
Tosafot on Chullin 90a:1:1.english: Evidently, the prohibition of sacrificial animals precedes - Rabbeinu Tam says: [This is] because at first, everything is flesh, and the flesh itself hardens afterward and turns white and becomes a sinew. And in the Kunteres [Rashi], he explained later that at first, when the sinew is formed, it is not on the socket, and [the prohibition] does not take effect until it comes and hardens on the socket. And even though now [the Gemara] means to say that the prohibition of the [sciatic] nerve does not take effect upon the prohibition of consecrated animals, [yet] upon the prohibition of a limb from a living animal — which is not as stringent as consecrated animals — it does take effect; and furthermore, because it is impossible for the prohibition of the [sciatic] nerve to exist in any other manner; and furthermore, because the prohibition of a limb from a living animal does not take effect until it is born, as [the Gemara] says at the end of our chapter (later, Chullin 103a): "For example, where it became a tereifah with the emergence of its majority," so that the prohibition of tereifah and the prohibition of a limb from a living animal take effect simultaneously:

Tosafot on Chullin 90a:3:1.hebrew: והא מתניתין דלא כרבי יהודה דקתני נוהג בשל ימין כו' - ה"מ למימר מדקתני "נוהג בשליל" ופליג ר' יהודה, אלא רישא דמלתא נקט:
Tosafot on Chullin 90a:3:1.english: But the mishna is not in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda, as it teaches [that it] applies to [the thigh] of the right [leg], etc. - [The Gemara] could have said [this] from [the fact] that [the mishna] teaches "[it] applies to a fetus," [regarding which] Rabbi Yehuda disagrees; rather, it cited the beginning of the statement:

Tosafot on Chullin 90a:5:1.hebrew: קדשים דאיסור כרת מי שמעת ליה - משמע דאפילו בשלמים ולאחר זריקה, דשרי אף לזרים, בעי למימר דלא חייל כלל איסור גיד ושרי באכילה, אע"ג דלאחר זריקה פקע איסור קדשים, מדלא אשכחן דחייל אלא במבכרת. ותימה: כיון דהשתא ליכא איסור קדשים, אע"ג דיכול לבא לידי איסור כרת, כגון אם אוכלו בטומאת הגוף, אמאי לא יחול איסור גיד, דאין כאן איסור חל על איסור, כדאמר בפרק ארבעה אחין (יבמות דף לב.) דאחות אשה מתלא תלי וקאי כו'? וי"ל: כיון דמחיים לא חייל איסור גיד, דאיכא איסור מוקדשין דיכול לבא לידי כרת על ידי פיגול ונותר וטמא, תו לא חייל איסור גיד לאחר שחיטה וזריקה, דבעינן שיחול מחיים איסור גיד, דומיא דיעקב שנשה לו גידו מחיים. וא"ת: ונימא מגו דאיתוסף איסור גיד לבני נח, איתוסף נמי לישראל? וי"ל: דהא דנאסר לבני נח, היינו דוקא לבני יעקב דקודם מתן תורה איקרו בני נח; ואפילו נאסר מתחלה לכל אומות העולם, הא אמר בפ' ארבע מיתות (סנהדרין דף נט.): כל מצוה שנאמרה לבני נח ולא נשנית בסיני, לישראל נאמרה ולא לבני נח; וא"כ לאחר מתן תורה שרו לכולהו, לבר מישראל. וא"ת: ונימא מיגו דאיתוסף איסור גיד לגבוה, דאסור להעלותו, איתוסף נמי להדיוט איסור אכילה? וי"ל: דאיכא למאן דאמר בסמוך: מחוברין יעלו:
Tosafot on Chullin 90a:5:1.english: [Regarding] sacrificial animals, which involve a prohibition of karet, did you hear [this]? - This implies that even with peace-offerings, and [even] after the sprinkling [of the blood], when [the meat] is permitted even to non-priests, [the Gemara] means to say that the prohibition of the sciatic nerve does not take effect at all and it is permitted to be eaten — even though after the sprinkling [of the blood] the prohibition of sacrificial meat has lapsed — since we do not find that [the prohibition of the sciatic nerve] takes effect [in sacrificial animals] except in the case of an animal giving birth to its firstborn. And this is puzzling: Since now there is no prohibition of sacrificial meat — even though one could come to a prohibition of karet, such as if he eats it while in a state of bodily impurity — why should the prohibition of the sciatic nerve not take effect, since there is no [issue here of a] prohibition taking effect upon [an existing] prohibition, just as [the Gemara] says in the chapter [entitled] Arba'ah Aḥin (Yevamot 32a) that [the prohibition of] a wife's sister remains suspended, etc.? And one can answer: Since during [the animal's] lifetime the prohibition of the sciatic nerve did not take effect — because there is the prohibition of consecrated [animals], which can lead to karet through piggul, notar, and impurity — the prohibition of the sciatic nerve no longer takes effect after slaughter and sprinkling [of the blood], because we require that the prohibition of the sciatic nerve take effect during [the animal's] lifetime, similar to Jacob, whose sciatic nerve was displaced during his lifetime. And if you ask: Let us say that since the prohibition of the sciatic nerve was added for the descendants of Noah, it was also added for Israel! And one can answer: That which it was prohibited to the descendants of Noah refers specifically to the sons of Jacob, who before the giving of the Torah were called "descendants of Noah"; and even if it was originally prohibited to all the nations of the world, [the Gemara] says in the chapter [entitled] Arba Mitot (Sanhedrin 59a): "Any commandment that was stated to the descendants of Noah and was not repeated at Sinai was stated [only] to Israel and not to the descendants of Noah." And if so, after the giving of the Torah it became permitted to all of them, except for Israel. And if you ask: Let us say that since the prohibition of the sciatic nerve was added with respect to the Most High [i.e., the altar], as it is forbidden to offer it up, a prohibition of eating was also added for an ordinary person! And one can answer: There is an opinion shortly [below] that [while] attached, they may be offered up:

Tosafot on Chullin 90a:6:1.hebrew: הכא במבכרת עסקינן דברחם קדוש - ובהדי הדדי קאתו, וקמ"ל דלא מבטל איסור קדשים החמור איסור גיד הקל מלחול עמו. וא"ת: והא איסור גיד לרבי יוחנן קדים, דאמר (לעיל חולין דף עה.): תלש חלב מבן תשעה חי, דחלבו כחלב בהמה, והדר אתא איסור מוקדשין דחמיר וחייל עליה, וא"כ לרבי יוחנן מוקדשין נוהגין בגיד מבעי ליה! ונראה דלר' יוחנן לא חייל איסור גיד ואיסור חלב עד שיצא לחוץ ממעי אמו לאויר העולם. וכן משמע, דבסוף פירקין (לקמן חולין דף קג.) קאמר רבי יוחנן גופיה, כשנטרפה עם יציאת רובה, דאיסור אבר ואיסור חלב ואיסור טרפה בהדי הדדי קאתו; אלמא דליכא איסור חל במעי אמו:
Tosafot on Chullin 90a:6:1.english: Here we are dealing with [an animal] giving birth to its firstborn, which becomes sanctified [at] the womb - And they [the two prohibitions] come simultaneously, and [the Mishnah] teaches us that the severe prohibition of consecrated [animals] does not preclude the lighter prohibition of the sciatic nerve from taking effect together with it. And if you ask: According to Rabbi Yochanan, doesn't the prohibition of the sciatic nerve precede [it], for he says (earlier, Chullin 75a) [that if] one tore off forbidden fat from a live nine-month [fetus], its fat is like the fat of an [ordinary] animal, and then the prohibition of consecrated [animals], which is severe, comes and takes effect upon it — and if so, according to Rabbi Yochanan, [the Mishnah] should have [stated that] consecrated [animals] are subject to [the prohibition of] the sciatic nerve! And it seems that according to Rabbi Yochanan, the prohibition of the sciatic nerve and the prohibition of forbidden fat do not take effect until it emerges outside from its mother's womb into the air of the world. And so it is implied, for at the end of our chapter (later, Chullin 103a), Rabbi Yochanan himself says, when it became a terefah upon the emergence of its greater part, that the prohibition of a limb [from a living animal], the prohibition of forbidden fat, and the prohibition of terefah come simultaneously; thus [we see] that no prohibition takes effect in its mother's womb:
